questions.learningObjective: apply the doctrine of personal jurisdiction to a concrete legal fact pattern
questions.stem: Consider this: A seller sued in a distant state challenges the court's power over them. The website was passive. Which statement best states the governing legal rule?

options.text: A single accidental contact always permits jurisdiction over the defendant for this case.
A defendant can never be sued where they have no office or employees in this instance.
options.misconception: treats physical presence as the only basis

options.text: Minimum contacts decides which courthouse within a state is convenient as the record shows.

Personal jurisdiction requires that the defendant have purposefully directed activities at the forum so that the lawsuit does not offend traditional notions of fair play and substantial justice in the present case.

Here the decisive point is minimum contacts and purposeful availment, so the result follows from that doctrine rather than from the surface appeal of a competing statement. Each distractor rests on a different mistake about how the doctrine operates.
questions.hint: Ask whether the defendant deliberately reached into the state. Keep the inquiry on minimum contacts and purposeful availment.
